Script to annotate significant GWAS snps

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rtracklayer)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(statgenGWAS)
library(here)
```

## Data loading
```{r}
annotation <- read_csv("/analyzed_data/GWAS_workshop/data/S_tort_YO1_2-1_Hap1_annotated.csv.gz")
head(annotation) #BLASTED each of the ST genes against AT (at the DNA level)
#could also do this at the protein sequence level, but chose DNA level since ST closely related to AT

#subject = gene identifier, .1 vs. .2 indicates the transcript form (if alternative splicing)
#perc_ID:score = info from the BLAST run 
```

Convert annotations to genomic ranges.
data form that makes it easy to take pieces of the genome and find overlaps 
```{r}
annotation_gr <- makeGRangesFromDataFrame(
	as.data.frame(annotation),
	seqnames.field = "chrom",
	keep.extra.columns = TRUE
)
annotation_gr
```

Get sig SNPs
```{r}
l2_height_GWAS <- readRDS(here("GWAS-traditional", "output", "l2.height.2025.06.09.gwas.pca.Rds" ))
l2_height_sig_snps <- l2_height_GWAS$signSnp[[1]]
l2_height_sig_snps

#allFreq = allele frequency
#effect size 
#standard error of effect size 
```

## Find genes overlapping significant SNPs

SNPs are treated as single-base positions. Need to convert chromosomes names.  Should check with Rishav about this.

```{r}
l2_height_snp_gr <- GRanges(
	seqnames = sprintf("Chr%02d", as.integer(as.character(l2_height_sig_snps$chr))),
	ranges = IRanges(start = l2_height_sig_snps$pos, width = 1)
)

l2_height_overlaps <- findOverlaps(l2_height_snp_gr, annotation_gr, maxgap = 0, ignore.strand = TRUE)
gene_info <- as_tibble(annotation_gr) %>%
	rename_with(~ paste0("gene_", .x))

l2_height_snp_gene_overlaps <- bind_cols(
	as_tibble(l2_height_sig_snps)[queryHits(l2_height_overlaps), ],
	gene_info[subjectHits(l2_height_overlaps), ]
)
l2_height_snp_gene_overlaps

#3 of the significant SNPs were in the boundaries of genes 
```
Note: if you want to include SNPs near protein coding portion of genes, increase maxgap

```{r}
l2_height_snp_gene_overlaps %>%
    select(snp, chr, pos, allFreq,pValue, gene_AGI, gene_At_symbol, gene_At_full_name, gene_At_short_description, gene_At_Curator_summary) %>% View()
```
